thesis: COPX is the largest pure-play copper equity ETF, tracking the Solactive Global Copper Miners Total Return Index across 40 producers with ~$7.26B in net assets at a 0.65% expense ratio. LME copper set an all-time high of ~$14,875/tonne on 2026-09-10 and is up ~50% year on year, while global mine supply may decline in 2026 for the first time since 2017 (Escondida suspension, Grasberg still impaired). COPX trades ~15% below its $99.99 52-week high because the White House deferred its Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision, not because the physical market loosened — miners fell 9.1% versus copper's 1.8% on 2026-09-10. The portfolio's 19.8x 2026E P/E compresses further on 2027 estimates if Deutsche Bank's $20,900/tonne 2027 average is anywhere near right; the risk is buying a high-beta cyclical (2.32 beta, 29.2% standard deviation) at a record input price.

drivers: Deutsche Bank's 2026-09-28 call plays out: $22,050/tonne by Q2 2027 and a $20,900 average for 2027, roughly $9–10/lb
Section 232 refined-copper tariff is formally adopted at 15% from 2027-01-01 rising to 30% in 2028, permanently widening the COMEX premium above $300/tonne
Global mined supply declines in 2026 for the first time since 2017 (Sprott) while Escondida and Grasberg disruptions persist
Portfolio EPS roughly doubles off 2026 levels and the market pays 12–14x forward rather than derating
US and Asian stockpiles reach ~71% of global supply, leaving the rest of the world scrambling for units into 2028

base_case.assumptions: Copper holds $6.50–7.50/lb (~$14,300–16,500/tonne) without a melt-up. ICSG refined usage grows to 29.2Mt in 2027, mine supply stays flat, and inventories remain tight but not critical. 2027 portfolio EPS grows ~30–45% and COPX re-rates to a mid-teens forward multiple, implying ~17–35% upside from $85.26. Grasberg reaches ~80% capacity by mid-2027 and Escondida labour talks settle without a prolonged strike.

risks: Cathode tariff is rejected or permanently exempted, releasing US-stockpiled metal back into the global market as the arbitrage trade unwinds
Copper mean-reverts toward the $10,710/tonne H1-2026 level Goldman originally modelled (~$4.50–5.00/lb), halving miner EPS
Aluminum substitution in wiring, busbars and grid applications accelerates at $6.50+/lb
China property contraction or stalled stimulus removes the demand floor — China consumes over half of global refined copper
Mid-cap concentration bites: single-asset failure at Hudbay, First Quantum or Teck hits the top weightings directly
Multiple derates simultaneously with earnings at a 2.32 beta, taking the fund back toward its $56.93 52-week low

catalysts.event: Escondida union contract vote and possible strike at the world's largest copper mine, following the 2026-09-23 fatality and progressive restart
Freeport-McMoRan Q3 2026 results and Grasberg ramp update (targeting ~65% capacity in H2 2026, ~80% by mid-2027)
Solactive semi-annual index reconstitution — rebalances the 40-name basket and the ~5% top weightings
Scheduled start of the Commerce-recommended 15% Section 232 tariff on refined copper imports, if the White House finalizes it
FY2026 results across the portfolio — first full year of realized copper above $6/lb, testing the operating-leverage thesis
Deutsche Bank's $22,050/tonne copper target date; also when US/Asian stockpile concentration is expected to peak
Second phase of the recommended tariff schedule — refined copper levy stepping up to 30%

key_risks: Buying a high-beta cyclical (2.32 beta vs S&P 500, 29.2% standard deviation) at an all-time-high copper price after a ~50% 12-month move
Tariff trade unwind — much of the 2026 rally is a policy artefact of US import pull-forward, and SMM notes the near-month arbitrage is already fading
Aluminum substitution caps the upside at sustained prices above $6.50/lb
China demand concentration — over half of global refined copper consumption, exposed to property and stimulus cycles
Mid-cap holding concentration: Hudbay, Teck and First Quantum are top weights and carry single-asset, permitting and resource-nationalism risk (DRC, Peru, Panama, Chile)
COPX owns equities, not metal — it can fall while copper rises, as it did on 2026-09-10 (-9.1% vs LME -1.8%)
0.65% expense ratio plus ~60-70bps tracking drag, unhedged CAD/GBP/PLN/JPY/AUD exposure, and lumpy semi-annual distributions unsuitable for income
